text: Follow one batch through the T L G O pilot plant, from graphite to a hydrogen tank.
In the pre G reactor, graphite is pre-oxidized with persulfate and phosphorus pentoxide in sulfuric acid.
In the fixing tank, the slurry is diluted, settles overnight, and the clear acid layer is decanted.
The filter press leaves wet pre G solids, and the acidic filtrate goes to waste treatment.
The solids are spread on trays and dried on a hot plate in the fume hood.
A second oxidation, with permanganate in strong acid, turns it into graphite oxide: T L G O.
Hydrogen peroxide goes in first. The batch then settles overnight and is decanted.
Then a hydrochloric acid wash removes the leftover manganese and metal ions.
Now the wash loop: filter the tank down, refill with clean water, and repeat, thirty-two times.
The permeate P H climbs from about one to four point four as the acid rinses out.
The washed G O soaks in D M F at ninety-five degrees, which also adds nitrogen for doping.
A flow-cell sonicator splits the stacked sheets apart, so dopants reach every layer.
Boric acid, the boron source, is stirred in at ninety-five degrees for four hours.
The spray dryer flashes off the solvent, leaving a fine, dry precursor powder.
In furnace one, at up to a thousand degrees under argon, boron and nitrogen lock into the carbon.
Potassium hydroxide is wet-mixed in at seventy degrees, then oven-dried for about four days.
Inside the inert line, furnace two activates the carbon at eight fifty, opening pores to store hydrogen.
Still under argon, the powder is pressed into one-gram pellets that pack densely into each tank.
Finally, the pellets are loaded, leak-tested, and outgassed at one hundred degrees under vacuum.
The result is P one hundred: two point seven five kilograms of B C K per tank.
In use, hydrogen splits and binds at boron and potassium sites.
Add heat, and the hydrogen is released, ready for the next cycle.
Sixteen steps, four quality checks, and up to five and a half percent hydrogen by weight.

Safety check. The main hazard here is a runaway reaction. Work only to approved dosing limits, with cooling, alarms and the vent route verified. If it starts to run away, raise the alarm, use only the approved remote safe-state action, and evacuate. Never improvise a quench.

Safety check. Watch for acid splash. Use closed transfer and splash protection, and know where the eyewash and shower are. If you are splashed, stop, alert your supervisor, and use the emergency wash right away.
Safety check. The filter press can hold stored pressure. Isolate it and confirm it is depressurized, drained and cool before opening. If something leaks unexpectedly, step back and restrict the area.

Safety check. Drying powder is an inhalation hazard. Work inside the fume hood with the exhaust running, and handle trays gently to avoid raising dust. If you are exposed, stop the task, leave the area, and tell your supervisor.

Safety check. Permanganate in strong acid can run away. Follow the approved addition rate and limits. If temperature or gas climbs fast, raise the alarm, use the approved remote safe state, and get out. Never add water to quench.

Safety check. The wrong chemical, or the wrong order, is the key risk. Confirm the identity and recipe revision before every addition, and keep incompatibles apart. If something reacts unexpectedly, stop the transfer and keep people clear.
Safety check. The wash skid lines can be under pressure. Isolate and verify zero energy before opening any connection. If a hose leaks or bursts, withdraw and restrict access until it is made safe.

Safety check. D M F is absorbed through the skin and is a reproductive toxin. This route is still under change review. Use closed handling, verified ventilation, and gloves selected from permeation data. If you are exposed, move away and follow the S D S decontamination steps.
Safety check. The sonicator is loud. Use the enclosure and the hearing protection set by the noise assessment. If you notice ringing or discomfort, step away and report it.
Safety check. Boric acid powder must not be inhaled. Charge it with source capture running, and keep the mixer guards in place. If dust escapes, stop and leave the area.

Safety check. Dry G O powder can decompose, burn, or cause a dust explosion. Stay within approved thermal limits, and clean only with approved methods. Never dry sweep or use compressed air. If there is a fire, raise the alarm and evacuate.

Safety check. The furnace runs at a thousand degrees, with hot off-gas. Never open or clear a hot, pressurized system. If the discharge blocks or pressure rises, keep clear and follow the approved safe-state procedure.

Safety check. Potassium hydroxide is corrosive and releases heat as it dissolves. This route is still under change review. Use splash protection and the approved order of addition. If it contacts skin or eyes, use the emergency wash immediately.
Safety check. Argon can displace oxygen in the inert line. If the oxygen alarm sounds, evacuate and keep everyone out. Call the planned rescue. Never attempt an unprotected rescue.
Safety check. The pellet press is a pinch point. Keep guards and interlocks in place, and lock out before clearing any jam. Never reach into moving equipment.
Safety check. Tank filling is not done alone unless the task is permitted, with documented check-ins. Use rated lifting aids for tanks. If a check-in is missed, the response procedure starts at once.
